question: Identify the new/current final ENA file and whether experiment_group_id and near_duplicate_family_id are retained at sequence–target-pair level
answer: Within data/raw the current authoritative ENA selected output is data/raw/ENA/review_v2/ena_selected_after_manual_review.csv (679 rows; 37 columns). It contains experiment_group_id (679/679 non-null; 25 unique; duplicates expected because many pairs share an experiment group) and near_duplicate_family_id (367/679 non-null = 54.05%; 56 unique; empty values coincide with missing near_duplicate_family_size and appear to mean no multi-member family / singleton). A newer processed file data/processed/ena/ena_aptamer_supplement_clean.csv (676 rows) retains near_duplicate_family_id but replaces experiment_group_id with supporting_experiment_group_ids only — so Stage S0 must not treat the processed clean table as having a dedicated experiment_group_id column unless that field is restored or derived.

curation_plan_implication: Use review_v2 selected CSV (or an updated processed export that keeps both IDs) as the ENA Stage S0 input; do not drop experiment_group_id during consolidation.

question: How do AptaDB aptamer.csv and protein.csv relate and can structured protein targets be joined?
answer: Most likely join: interaction.csv is the bridge table. Join aptamer.csv.Apta_index = interaction.csv.Apta_index and for protein targets interaction.csv.TargetID = protein.csv.Uni-port ID. Evidence: official AptaDB About page lists separate Interaction/Aptamer/Protein downloads; publication states Aptamer IDs and Target IDs (UniProt for proteins) identify interactions; local interaction.csv has 1350 rows with Apta_index and TargetID; all 194 protein UniProt IDs appear as TargetID; all 639 Target chemistry=Protein interactions match protein.csv; 1256/1293 aptamers appear in interaction (37 aptamers lack interaction rows). Relationship is many-to-many (48 aptamers with >1 target; 228 targets with >1 aptamer). Confidence: high.
evidence: Join audit counts; example Apta_1/Apta_2 → A6MI22 Tat protein; website download table confirms Interaction export.
remaining_uncertainty: Molecule/Cell/Other TargetIDs are not in protein.csv (expected); molecule.csv/cell.csv/other.csv not present locally; 37 aptamers without interaction rows.
curation_plan_implication: AptaDB protein targets can be attached via interaction.csv without waiting for free-text E5 extraction; still need molecule/cell tables if non-protein targets are required.

question: Interpret precision_selex_against_kpc2_paper/extracted_data.xlsx schema and sequence columns
answer: Workbook has one sheet Sheet1 with multi-row header and blank spacer rows; merged cells present. True headers are on rows 2–3; data on even rows starting row 4 (20 aptamer records XK-1…XK-20). Columns A–J: Aptamer-ID; Sequences of N40 from 5' to 3' (primary 40-nt DNA sequence); ΔG (n40); Truncated sequences of library from 5' to 3' (construct DNA); ΔG (construct); round4 library2 count; round4 library1 count; round8 library2 count; round8 library1 count (heading incomplete); Target (=KPC-2). Row1 'Repeat times' is a merged layout label spanning count columns F–J not a per-row field. Sequences are ssDNA A/C/G/T without U; no punctuation inside inspected sequence cells. Documented in README_extracted_data.md (Yu et al. 2021 Talanta).
evidence: ZIP/XML cell layout inspection; README column table; sample XK-1/XK-2 rows.
remaining_uncertainty: Column I heading incomplete (library 1 inferred); 'truncated sequences' exact primer boundaries not fully specified.
curation_plan_implication: Include as manually extracted DNA eval/corpus candidate using column B as primary sequence and column D as construct provenance; do not silently T→U without marking computational transcription.
